newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 29.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on its front page on July 29:
WASHINGTON - Nearly 40 percent of home health care services provided to frail Americans under the Medicare program are unjustified, federal investigators said.

WASHINGTON - The military chief of the Air Force abruptly resigned Monday, amid growing tensions with civilian authorities over responsibility for guarding against last year's terrorist truck bombing in Saudi Arabia.

WASHINGTON - The White House and congressional Republicans announced a tenative agreement on the final details of a long-sought, five-year plan to balance the budget, revamp Medicare, and provide the first major tax cut since the early 1980s.
WASHINGTON - The number of murders in the nation's capital and Maryland's adjoining Prince George's County hit 10-year lows during the first half of the year.

BOSTON - Massachusetts Gov. William Weld quit his job to focus national attention on the Washington rules that allow one man -- Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms -- to block his confirmation as ambassador to Mexico.
WASHINGTON - Yong Yun, a Washington businessman who helped renovate D.C. Mayor Marion Barry's home, pleaded guilty in federal court to making a false statement on a bank loan application.
